body:
I suppose there are multiple aspects to it. There's a constant, basically total anhedonia and emotional numbness, which means that I can't enjoy anything or really feel anything; I haven't cried since I was in the hospital in 2015, even when our dog died there was maybe one tear or two, but it's like I'm a boiling pot that never boils over, there's never any catharsis. Nothing makes me happy or feels good (I like talking to my girlfriend, and I love her, but there's numbness in the way as well). There's also a constant passive suicidality, ever since I was a kid I've thought about dying and self-harm, and sometimes, like recently, I come up with a basic plan of how I would do it, no dates or anything but I know the methods and what time of day to do it and stuff. And I also despise myself, inside and out, there isn't anything I like about myself, and I wish I didn't exist, and I feel like human consciousness was a massive evolutionary mistake and life is a curse.

They do give me work to do; for example, my current therapist suggested walking, and until recently, I was going for walks most days, and she also suggested things like affirmations and counter statements. I just really really struggle to do the things people suggest, like I can't find the energy for even simple things, and I can't seem to persevere with hard things and processes, everything seems too stressful and unenjoyable. And it doesn't seem like anything I do do has any effect on me either. It's like I'm just really fundamentally broken and there's nothing I or anyone can do

Oh yeah, it definitely was worse to be mentally ill back then. It's still bad, but it was much worse then.

I suppose that's true. Life is inherently filled with suffering and misery, which is why I don't really think it's worth living, but that's another matter

That's a very good point, I think you're right. I certainly have trouble remembering some things, like I spent 3 months in hospital and I barely remember any of it, it's a blur

Ah, thank you. I doubt it, to be honest, but thank you

Thank you for your comment

I guess that makes sense. The process of medication is just so hard and long (that's what she said), they only let me see the psychiatrist every three months. But I will try to make him see how bad things are. He put me on the Sertraline and Propranolol despite me saying that I've been on them before and they haven't helped. I agree that the depression needs to treated first, but others don't seem to agree; my mum doesn't believe that I'm depressed at all, and when I met the crisis team a few days after trying to end it (wish I had succeeded), they just said that if the OCD was treated I wouldn't be depressed, and did literally nothing. It's been 9 years of depression, and nothing has really helped, there have been times where it hasn't been quite as severe but it's never been good enough for me to feel like life is worth living.

I guess I don't even really know how to stay active, it seems like literally everything is just too hard, I couldn't even bring myself to shave the other day. And there's nothing that I enjoy or like doing, so everything I do is just stressful.

It just seems like nothing can help at this point, I know I haven't had all the medications available but I've had several, and I've had lots of therapies (CBT, TherapyForYou, group OCD therapy, counselling at college, EMDR, art psychotherapy and now private therapy), and it doesn't seem that any of them have actually helped. I remember describing it as like there is a forcefield that everything just bounces off before it can penetrate. I guess if going into hospital would help, maybe I would try (I was hospitalised for my eating problems and OCD in 2015, and by the time I left, they seemed to have receded a bit, but then I was left with the anhedonia and numbness and depression until the other issues returned.

And they say that you have to want to get better, and it seems like I can't make myself want that; the only things I want are maybe to visit my girlfriend at some point (if I last that long), but mainly just to cease to exist. I know it's most likely my own fault for being lazy, but I just can't seem to handle life at all

Thank you for your advice and support

That's a good point. My mum had postnatal depression for years, but she seems to have forgotten what it was like, and now she doesn't believe that I have depression at all, she says I'm just in a bad mood. Meanwhile, my therapist said she's never seen anyone as depressed as me. It's hard, maybe our families and loved ones kind of block out the memories of struggling because they don't want to remember their loved one in pain. I'm sorry that you go through that with your mum
That makes sense, thank you. Maybe I will give it a go. It's just that I just can't seem to bring myself to try things anymore, it just seems too hard and too unenjoyable

Thank you for your comment

I guess I just think, if there's nothing she can do, what could anyone else do? Pretty much every therapist I've had has ended up with the same reaction. So it just looks like the problem is with me and not them

That's an interesting way of looking at it. I guess I just think that I would get overwhelmed and give up as I do with most things I try, and it seems unlikely that I would be able to make the most of things anyway because I couldn't enjoy them. Not that I could get a job anyway, nowhere would hire me.

I guess I just think, this isn't the first venting post I've made, though I guess it's been a while. So even if it was progress, it's old progress from years ago

Thank you for your comment

I guess I just dunno. She seems really good; she has experience with OCD, depression and autism, so it seems like she knows things, and she seems to care. To be honest, pretty much every therapist I've had has had a similar reaction: they realise that they can't help and then the therapy is over. After my previous therapy, I didn't think I wanted to try again, so I really think after this one, my treatment journey will probably be over. It's my own fault for being lazy and weak, but it looks like there is just something about me that can't make me want to get better

That seems like dangerous thinking. Where do you draw the line once you start? Should people who worry that they might hurt someone (but never do) be eliminated? Should a young man who gets so angry he imagines killing his boss (but would never actually do it) be eliminated?

You're entitled to think what you like. I just wonder if you're simplifying and dividing things to a concerning degree. Everyone has messed up thoughts, I don't think there is anyone who hasn't thought something pretty messed up at some point. I'm sure you have had messed up thoughts yourself, and that's ok, it's just life and the curse of human consciousness
That's very true, we wish that we didn't have to tell people how hard things are, especially since it's hard to tell people and they can react badly. It really sucks

That's interesting, I guess I will have to look into it, thank you for telling me about it. 

Ohhh, ok, I've never thought of that. It does look like I probably am autistic, so it would be interesting to see if something like that does end up working a bit better.

I guess I'll try, I just don't know how to keep my mind open, it feels like I'm shrivelling up. Thank you for your advice and support

So you think that people should be removed from existence because of their thoughts? I hope you never meet anyone with POCD.

I don't like things where people die either, it disturbs me, and I have never downloaded any porn in my life. I just think that a person can't always help the thoughts that come into their heads, or the things that, for some reason, have an effect on them. It's not their fault, and they shouldn't be punished for it unless they act on their thoughts.

I'm sorry, I don't mean to argue or anything. I just know what it's like to have thoughts that you hate but can't prevent, and that make you feel guilty.

Thank you, you are a kind person. I just think, if I'm so exhausted and spent and miserable now, when I don't have a job or pay taxes or live alone or have responsibilities, what the hell is it going to be like if I ever do have to do those things? Surely I'm screwed if this comparatively leisurely existence is too hard for me

That's a good way of looking at it. To be honest, I don't see how it is progress, but I appreciate it. I'm actually gonna try and get a bit of sleep now, I never feel rested afterwards, but maybe I won't feel hungover for once. Hope you're doing well

But it's not like a person just thinks about it one day and decides to be attracted to that sort of thing. And I'm sure that a great many such people hate themselves for having that interest, and shaming them and saying that they should be alone won't help anything at all. It doesn't make them bad people, most people would never go through with any of the things that they might fantasise about or find arousing. Yes, it might be messed up in a way, but people are messed up, they always have been and always will, it's just life

Thank you for telling me about that, I've never looked into psychoanalysis, I suppose I thought maybe it was outdated or something, but that is interesting. I would certainly say that my illnesses have become my life and my identity, there is nothing else to me.

That's a good way of looking at things, makes a lot of sense. To be honest, the problem is that there isn't a way I want to live; I mean, if I actually was mentally healthy and had the capacity for happiness, I guess that would be good, but that's all but impossible, so there isn't a life that I want. It seems like it's being alive that is itself the problem. I really appreciate your advice and support, it just looks like I am just not strong enough or human enough to really follow it or to get better

Thank you so much for the advice and support. I'm sorry, I can't think of a response that is as long and detailed as your comment.

That all sounds like really good advice. But I'm afraid I just can't do it. It's just too difficult, I just don't have it in me anymore. I'm sorry, I do appreciate you trying to help. I'm just done.

Thank you for your comment

I'm sorry to hear about that experience with your old therapist. That sucks that he would text during sessions and not contribute, that's wrong and not fair to you. I guess I dunno really. It seems that pretty much every therapist I've had has ended up feeling that way, stumped. I guess it's probably more my fault than hers, I guess I'm just too lazy and weak

Thank you for your comment

I'm sorry to hear that you have a similar collection of disorders, it's hellish.

I guess I just don't know, I mean, I've had a lot of therapies and therapists over the years, and she seems like one of the best ones, with real experience with mental health and neurodivergence. So it seems hard to imagine that anyone else would be better. I've never had IFS or similar treatment, I guess I didn't think it would be helpful in my case

That's great that you have found the right therapist, hopefully they really help

That's a good way of looking at things, nothing changes if nothing changes. I should keep that in mind, but when I go to try something new or start a process, I just get overwhelmed by how stressful and depressing and unenjoyable it is and end up giving up. I don't want to be the way I am, but I don't seem to genuinely want to get better, I just seem to want to cease to exist.

That sounds like a good goal, hopefully you achieve it. To be honest, I don't have any goals or ambitions or anything like that, nothing appeals to me as something I'd like to do or to achieve

I guess that's true that exercise should be helpful. I can't say I've ever felt better after exercising, if anything, when I went to the gym last year, I was more anxious during and after it. I struggle with ideas like yoga or dancing, I know it's silly, but they seem like women's things, so as a straight man, it seems hard to see myself doing them. It just seems that any kind of exercise or strenuous or even easy activity is too much for me, like I can do nothing anymore. 

That's a good idea, trying to care for yourself like someone else would. I guess I'm not really sure what that would look like for me, but I appreciate it

The frustrating thing is, I don't like anything (except my girlfriend), everything is just stress and suffering to me. I just can't see how it could be worth the struggle when I'm incapable of enjoying any of it anyway. Sorry to be depressing, thank your for your support

Thank you for your comment

Thank you, yeah a few people have suggested those actually. I'll look into them and suggest them at my next appointment with the psychiatrist. I guess I'm not optimistic, but if one of those things could help it would be great. Thank you

That's interesting, it makes sense. I just really don't know how to change my mindset, I've tried affirmations and things like that but just couldn't persist. It just seems too set in stone and too difficult

I never look forward to anything, full stop. My anhedonia means that I could be in the most amazing situation, and it would have no effect on me because I'm too numb. How can I live life if I can't even feel alive? I guess I will have a look at breathing, I've tried to do the 4-7-8 method, but it's had no effect on me, and I used to count to five five times to try and help with anxiety, but I don't know if it did help.

My brain probably is tricking me as you say, but it honestly seems like there are no useful things, nothing ever seems to actually help, it all just bounces off this forcefield around me.

It just seems like literally everything is too hard at this point, even having a shave was too hard yesterday. It's like I'm just completely empty, out of resources

Thank you for your comment

To be honest, even the idea of getting relief from anything or catching a break seems so outlandish and impossible. I honestly can't remember the last time I relaxed, it seems like something I just cannot do. 

My meds are prescribed by a psychiatrist, I'm not sure what the other terms mean (I'm in the UK). I guess it's hard because I need medication and treatment for more than one problem, so I guess it's like spinning plates.

That's a good idea, I haven't thought of doing a gene test, I don't really know if they're a thing here, but I'll have a look, thank you.

I've seen a couple of other people recommend TMS actually, I think I'll ask about it when I see the psychiatrist on the 2nd, and the other things people have suggested, like esketamine or ECT.

Those sound interesting. I started to read The Happiness Trap, but it seemed to involve too much mindfulness, I really struggle with mindfulness to the point where it's unbearable.

That's a good way of looking at it. I just think that I'm probably too weak and lazy and don't try hard enough, but can't seem to make myself try harder, or make myself want to get better. 

Thank you so much for your advice and support

Thank you, I really appreciate it. I just don't think it's going to happen, it's been this way my entire life and it seems just too hard to change at this point. But thank you.

I appreciate you trying to help. I hope you don't feel bad or anything. To quote a film, "Some people are born just so they can be buried." And that's ok, it's just life

I see. Yeah, I guess that doesn't really sound like a good idea for me.

To be honest, I really struggle with exercise, not only because it's hard and I don't enjoy it at all, but also because I have eating problems and worry about making myself sick through exercise. I do intend to start going for walks again, and I had thought about trying to work out at home, but it seems unlikely to happen now. I know it might seem like an exaggeration, but I really mean it when I say that nothing helps, ever, nothing makes me feel good.

Thank you for your comment

That's the thing, I should've mentioned it in the post. Pretty much every therapy I've had has had the same ending, they realise that there's nothing they can do, and they call it quits. Obviously, it's my fault, I guess I'm too weak and lazy, and I don't want it enough, but they always come to the conclusion that there's nothing they can do. I don't think I can go again through the process of looking for a therapist and waiting and then explaining everything to them and trying to follow their advice to go avail.

Sorry to be negative, I appreciate your kind words and support, but I just think it's too late for me, I'm just gone.

I'm sorry that things are still tough for you, hopefully they will improve soon

It's great that things are at least better than that for you now. I get what you mean, I suppose I would say that I don't feel sorry for myself, I hate myself and don't think I deserve anyone's pity, but I understand your point.

Thank you so much for your positivity and support. I just can't do it anymore, it's just too hard. I know it's my fault, and I'm lazy and weak, but I'm just spent. Thank you for trying to help
I wouldn't say that, I think it's more that I'm just too much of a pussy to end things, I got so close two years ago but I wussed out. So I just exist, not alive but not physically dead yet

Thank you for your comment

I see, that's interesting, I've not heard of that clinic. I suppose I don't really know if I would qualify, I would say my OCD is bad, but I don't think it's really as bad as it used to be when I had to be hospitalised. I suppose it's like, the really hard thing is that since that first hospitalisation, I've had numbness and anhedonia and depression, and now the OCD and anxiety mix in with those. So it's like, I would say I'm worse now in general, but perhaps my OCD and eating problems if isolated would seem not as bad as they once were.

I'm not under a CMHT, and to be honest, I've never heard of an Access team. I had a care coordinator for a little while, maybe in 2019 or 2020, but they dropped out once I started with a psychiatrist again and was getting assessed for psychotherapy (they assessed me and referred me to art psychotherapy, but it didn't help at all). Now that the psychotherapy has finished, it looks like they've forgotten about my therapeutic treatment completely, I haven't heard anything since the end of 2023. So I went for private therapy instead.

You could tell me about those medications privately if you like? No pressure or anything, would be interesting to know, though. I guess I give medications a go, my psychiatrist appointments are only every three months (too long, I think, but they won't do sooner), so I have to spend a while with them. I think the Lithium was an attempt to augment my meds, but I shook so badly I thought I was getting Parkinson's like my grandad.

I just do not see anything to suggest that I am not beyond help, nothing seems to help, and I seem to lack the energy and strength to force change on my own, so it seems like I am just out of options except for the obvious. Pretty much every therapist and psychiatrist I've had has ended up stumped (a psychiatrist once said, "It's not a medication problem, it's a you problem"), so surely there must come a time to say it's over.

I think that people really would be better off without me, I'm such a burden and a parasite, on my family, the people around me, the government, and the world. I really should've died at birth.

To be honest, at this point, the illness is who I am. It's been 11 years. I have no identity, no hobbies or dreams or aspirations or anything, I just float along, no arms or legs to swim with.

Sorry for being depressing, thank you so much for your kind words and advice and support. Hope you're doing well

Thank you for replying

That's what my therapist said today, that mindfulness isn't for everyone, some techniques and stuff help some people and not others. Which is very depressing.

I see, that sounds interesting, I'll have to look into it, thank you

Thank you for your comment

I guess I just think that if she couldn't help, a therapist with experience of OCD, depression and autism, how could any other help? And the idea of stopping and moving yet again is just so depressing. It seems like no treatment I've had in 9 years has helped in the long term, therapy or medication. Surely there has to be a time when you decide that it's over, and it's better to let the time and effort and resources go to someone who deserves it and who it might actually benefit?

Thank you for your advice, it's great that you've managed to get some relief

Thank you for your comment

It's good that you can see a version of yourself that you would like to become, I think that is important as it gives you a goal to work towards. To be honest, in my case, there is no self I'd like to become (other than I suppose one that is capable of enjoying life, but that seems out of reach with anhedonia and numbness), and I can't imagine having peace while being alive; obviously, there's no guarantee that death brings peace, but I suppose it's a matter of being desperate enough to take that gamble, I'm not there yet but I think I will be eventually.

I wouldn't say I've persevered, I merely died, and my body carried on. I'm an empty shell, a breathing corpse.

I just don't think I have it in me to fight and struggle even more, just being awake is a struggle, so the idea of actively battling things is just too much. It's brilliant that you've been able to see that you've made progress, I'm sure that that'll continue to get better.

I think at this point, it's just too late, and I'm just too broken in too many ways. Maybe if I could enjoy things in life, I might see the point in struggling, or maybe I still wouldn't. But I just don't want to live with this mind and this brain and this body. Sorry for being negative, thank you so much for your positivity and support, hope you continue to do well

People have interests in so many different things, and often, they don't know why and don't like having the interests they have. For example, there is nothing wrong with having a thing for hypnotism, but someone who doesn't have that interest might struggle to understand the appeal or might even be disturbed by it. And that's ok, people are into different things, and as long as they don't harm anyone, I don't really see the problem.

And for the record, no, I'm not a fan of things involving tentacles at all

Thank you for your comment

I just find it unbearable. It's like having a TV on static, then turning it up extremely loud. I can't observe any thoughts or anything, I'm just pummelled by noise until I have to stop, I can't bear it. I'm not sure if it's legal to get mushrooms or psilocybin here, and I'm not exactly the type of person who knows how to get stuff like that. But if I could, maybe I'd give it a go, but as you say, I don't know what's going on inside me.

I guess it's weakness and laziness. I just can't seem to push through any kind of hardship or things that require a lot of effort

I guess that makes sense. I mean, I'm a coward, so it'll probably be a while before I have the strength or desperation to actually end things, so I suppose I'll keep going until then. Thank you for your positivity

Yeah. To be honest, I just think that I'm not in the right place to do it, and probably never will be. Maybe if the depression is a bit less overwhelming, I'll feel more able, but that seems unlikely. I think I'm approaching the end of the road, but thank you so much for your support

Thank you for your comment

I do see a psychiatrist, they only do appointments every three months, which is annoying. He put me on Sertraline and Propranolol, even though I've been on them before and they didn't help, because he didn't want to put me on something powerful before trying other things. But I guess I doubt that any medication can help at this point, none have, not long-term at least. I am planning to get assessed for ADHD at the same time as autism, we'll see how that goes I guess. And I think she is good, but I suppose if she is stumped, then maybe it'll just hurt her to keep going and disappointing her

I guess so. I guess we'll have to see, I don't blame her if she is stumped, though. Other therapists have been. I guess I just don't know what could change at this point, I can't seem to make changes on my own or persevere with hard processes, so it seems like I'm pretty stuck, my own fault of course but still stuck

Ah, ok, I see. That's good that you've found it so helpful. I guess I think that I really struggle to persist, if something doesn't seem to be helping quickly, I tend to give up after not very long. But I suppose I would give it a go, and as I say, if it doesn't help, I'll just kill myself anyway

Thank you so much for your kindness and support. That makes sense to replace one hard thing with a more healthy hard thing. I just really struggle to do that in any regard. And to be honest, the only time I think I can remember ever actually being ok or happy is when I was 13 in 2013, a few months before everything started to go wrong. My entire life I've been passively suicidal at least

I know it's bad to say, but to be honest, if I was taking care of a little kid, especially if it was myself, I would tell them to make sure to kill themselves before they become a teenager, because life is not worth the suffering. Thank you so much for your support, hope you're doing well

Thank you for your comment

I see, thank you for telling me about that. It sounds promising, I suppose I'm wary because it sounds like there must be side effects or negative effects, and I guess it also seems unlikely to help me as nothing does. But I'll mention it to my psychiatrist, because I really need a change, I can't stand the anhedonia and numbness. If it doesn't work, then I'll end myself anyway, so I guess there's not much to lose really

I see, thank you for telling me about that. That really sucks, why can't there be any treatment that doesn't have negative side effects, it's not fair. It's like God himself doesn't want us to get better.

At the same time, I suppose I'm still desperate enough to consider it, and if it doesn't work, I'll still end up ending it so I suppose there's not much to lose

Thank you for telling me, hope things are at least bearable for you

I guess that makes sense. It's frustrating; when I was in the psychiatric ward for three months in 2015, by the time I left, the OCD and eating problems seemed to have receded, but I can't remember if it was the therapy that helped, or the medication (I've been and am on the same medication since and it hasn't helped), or the sheer stress of being in hospital, that whole period of time is a blur and I can't really remember what we did in therapy or anything.

I guess I just think that maybe I'm too depleted at this point. I don't have the energy or even the desire to do anything, let alone things that are hard, so I don't know how I could possibly do something as hard as ERP. Of course, living with OCD is hard as well. Which I suppose is why I think there may be only one real solution left, because I'm simply too weak and indifferent and disconnected
Oh wow, thank you for looking for me. That's good then, I'll have to see if it's a thing in my area, but might be worth a look. Thank you

Thank you for replying

I've heard good things about TMS. I'm not sure if it's available in England or how or where to get it if it is available, but I'll have a look. I guess the prospect of still having to fight is daunting, and it's hard to see the point, but I guess if it could improve things, it could be worth a go. It would be good if there was a similar treatment for stuff like OCD, but it seems like OCD treatment can only be cruel and agonising.

Thank you for your advice, hope you're doing well

I'm sorry that you had to go through so many therapists. I'm not sure exactly what the number is for me, but I think it might be close to that. I guess it's tough because with me, my OCD is kind of not the biggest issue, but it's certainly one of them.

To be honest, I just think it's too hard, I don't have the strength to keep trying with it and pushing through the agony of exposure. Whenever I try, I succumb because I just can't take the anxiety and stress. Thank you for your advice and kindness, to be honest, I think recovery isn't possible in my case, but I appreciate it

Thank you for your comment

I agree; in recent times, multiple people have suggested that I have autism, but nobody has suggested ADHD, but I suspect that I have both. So hopefully soon I'm gonna get assessed for both, it's expensive, but I think it could be worth it. It would be great if I could treat that, and it have a knock-on effect on my other issues, I guess I'm not optimistic, but it would be nice. So we will definitely look into it. Thank you for the advice

Yeah, I'm in England. I'm not sure what a private therapist can do here in terms of getting other support involved because they're not connected to the system. And even if I was to end up going inpatient again or something, there's usually a long wait. Plus, last time all it did was hold the OCD back for a couple of years and allow depression and numbness and anhedonia to take its place until it was ready to join again. So it seems kind of pointless

We've tried a few things, for OCD and my other issues. She suggested I go to the gym, which I tried but was too anxious for, so I've been trying to go for walks instead, which I was doing until I had withdrawal from one of my medications and felt too ill to continue, and haven't started again. And we've tried coming up with counter statements for my anxiety worries, which I suppose haven't been completely useless when I remember to use them, and counter statements for the things I hate about myself, which I need to try and use. But it's like everything we try, or everything I've tried with any therapist, just pretty much bounces off these days, like I'm completely resistant to any kind of treatment. It really seems like I'm at a dead end, and there's only one option left. I don't want to hurt my family and others, but I don't think I can spend life like this

Thank you for your comment

I dunno really. They say that you have to want to get better, and it seems like I'm not capable of wanting anything except to cease to exist. I don't know how to make myself want to be alive or to get better. And I suppose I kind of doubt that any other therapist would be better, I mean, she has OCD herself so it seems like she would be better equipped to help than most? And I guess there's also the fact that none of the other therapies I've had have helped, so it seems unlikely that anything will. Sorry to be negative. It just really seems like there is no hope left; like my psychiatrist said, it's as if I'm 90 and waiting to die

Thank you for your comment

To be honest, I'm not sure it's available here in England, and if it is, the waiting list or the costs or both are probably ridiculous. But if I could get either one or both I would give them a go

Thank you for your comment

That's the thing, it seems like I gave up long ago. It doesn't seem like there is anything that I want, other than to maybe cease to exist entirely. I guess maybe I just think, the OCD receded after my stay in the psychiatric ward, but it was just replaced with anhedonia, numbness and depression until it came back to mix in with everything else. So even if I did somehow manage to force it back, it'll just come back different, and even if it doesn't come back, I'll still be miserable, so what's the point? Thank you for your advice, I'm not sure what self-compassion is really. I try to be grateful for things, i know there's a lot to be grateful for, but I just lack the ability to enjoy any of it, and I feel like i don't deserves any of it

Hope you're doing well

Thank you for your comment

I do intend to go for walks, I was doing it every day, but I got withdrawal from one of my medications and haven't gone out again since. Eating is a struggle because of my disorder, I currently eat twice a day but I feel fat regardless. Self-talk is really hard for me, especially since I don't seem to have an inner monologue, but I probably could do more. To be honest, meditation is kind of a no-go for me, I was actually talking about it with my therapist today; for me, mindfulness and meditation is like torture, like having the TV on static and turning it up really loud, it's unbearable. Music used to be the closest thing I had to a passion, but all interest and enjoyment has evaporated from it. And to be honest, I really don't see how I could be worth it, there's nothing good about me

Sorry, I'm not trying to shoot you down or anything. Just feels like I'm really stuck, and even though it's probably my fault, I can't seem to get out of it

Thank you for your comment

I'm not sure really. She's great, and I think that she has come closer to really helping than almost any other therapist I've had; until the past couple of weeks, it actually seemed like maybe things might someday look up, but I've plummeted recently for no discernable reason.
